has cited version text updated March 2026

has quoted text Adaptive designs get no specific treatment in the NICE manual (PMG36, updated March 2026), so a [health technology assessment](/concept/health-technology-assessment) applies its general evidence and uncertainty requirements. The DSU checklist TSD 7 asks for early-stopped trials to enter a synthesis unadjusted when the stopping rules were prespecified. TSD 7's advice concerns pooling trials in a synthesis. Where an economic evaluation rests on a single adaptive trial, the FDA guidance and ACE point towards reporting estimates that allow for the design alongside the conventional ones.

citation of NICE PMG36 in concept added-therapeutic-value, Concept Architecture, 28f8fc

https://healtheconomics.wiki/ontologies/heiro/HEIRO_6000984
Type guidance citation record
cites guidance document NICE technology appraisal and highly specialised technologies guidance, the manual (PMG36)
concerns wiki concept Added Therapeutic Value
has citation field Concept Architecture
has cited version date 2026-03
has cited version text last updated March 2026
has mention count 0
has quoted text A cost-effectiveness system asks a different question. The NICE manual (PMG36, last updated March 2026) turns clinical effectiveness into QALYs and costs and judges the [ICER](/concept/icer) against its [cost-effectiveness threshold](/concept/cost-effectiveness-threshold). Below a most plausible ICER of 25,000 GBP per QALY the decision normally rests on the estimate, and above 35,000 GBP the committee needs an increasingly stronger case. The clinical gain enters through the QALY estimate and is traded against cost, so modest added benefit can be recommended at a low enough price.

has quoted text Population burden multiplies how many people are affected by how badly each is affected. Health technology assessment usually cares about the second factor separately, as severity. The NICE technology appraisal manual (PMG36, last updated 31 March 2026) defines severity as the future health lost by people living with the condition with standard care in the NHS, and measures it by [absolute shortfall](/concept/absolute-shortfall) and [proportional shortfall](/concept/proportional-shortfall) in QALYs against the general population of the same age and sex. has quoted text Every funded service displaces something else under a fixed budget. The NICE technology appraisal manual (PMG36, last updated 31 March 2026) states that, given the fixed budget of the NHS, the appropriate maximum acceptable ICER is that of the opportunity cost of programmes displaced by new, more costly technologies. The same reasoning applies in reverse. If an existing service costs far more per QALY than the care displaced at the margin, withdrawing it and reinvesting the money raises population health.

has quoted text In an economic evaluation, the chosen perspective decides which third-party effects are counted, so an effect that is external to one perspective may be internal to another. The reference case in the NICE manual (PMG36, last updated 31 March 2026) counts health effects for patients and, when relevant, other people (mainly carers), while costs are those of the NHS and personal social services. Benefits to other government bodies, such as reduced crime from treatments for drug misuse, are considered only in non-reference-case analyses agreed with the Department of Health and Social Care.
